## Highlights

- Highlights of this week:

## Hot Spot Isue in the Confocal System

The was problem when trying to image the sample with the 640 nm (Cy5) excitation. 
There was a strong signal in the center which is not scanned and probably a back reflection 
from a surface in the system. The issue is fixed now.

## Hot spot Issue in Confocal System

There was an issue with the dichroic mirror in the confocal system that caused a hot spot in the image for 640 nm excitation. I just change to another dichroic mirror and the hot spot issue is fixed. Now I can 
get a clean image for iSCAT-LSCM colocalization.

![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.08.31 (Amir Fathi - Fix LSCM, Z-Stacking)\hot-spot-line.png)

## iSCAT Fringe Suppression by Z Stacking

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.08.31 (Amir Fathi - Fix LSCM, Z-Stacking)\iscat-z-stacking.png)

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

During the experiment, I found that the interference fringes in the iSCAT image can be suppressed when 
I am fine-tuning the focus manually. Just to roughly demonstrate the effect, I start the 
acquisition and keep fine-tuning the focus. Then, offline, I average those frames. The frame range 
is highlighted on each image. One idea could be using a piezo stage in open loop to modulate 
the focus within the exposure time. The data will be inherently averaged on the image sensor 
at pixel level. This can even be implemented with TAG lens which can run at tens of kHz for 
high speed imaging. I have also added a video in my report to show the effect of fringe suppression by Z stacking.

:::

:::

## SLB Background Correction

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.08.31 (Amir Fathi - Fix LSCM, Z-Stacking)\slb-bg-correction.png)

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

I can clean the background for the SLB images. There three steps involved. 
First correct for lateral shift, then correcting for flat field, finally temporal rolling
background correction. Although, I can significantly correct the background, still 
the iscat profile is challenging for tracking. One path forward is using a custom 
detector in TrackPy not default one which is for a Gaussian profile. 

:::

:::
